purpose: Compare all 18 marine fish and 3 crustacean name strings printed in MCTEP EIS Table 2.27 with exact-name WoRMS records and focused Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes records. Keep original strings, accepted-name mappings, and any possible spelling variants distinct from specimen identity.

worms.provider: World Register of Marine Species (WoRMS), Aphia exact-name API
worms.noResultMeaning: HTTP 204 means this exact query returned no Aphia record in this request. It is not proof that the name is nonexistent, that no synonym exists, or that the EIS specimen is misidentified.

catalogOfFishes.provider: California Academy of Sciences, Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes
catalogOfFishes.onlineVersionAsSeen: Catalog species pages show online versions updated between 10 June and 21 September 2026.
catalogOfFishes.scope: Focused checks of the accepted-name and related-name entries needed to assess the material spelling variants and current combinations; this was not a morphological re-identification.

decision.disposition: Store this as a nomenclatural crosswalk only. Preserve every MCTEP source spelling and rank alongside any accepted-name result. Keep all rows out of Bangwit species projections until the study's identifications, per-site allocation, provenance and item-specific reuse rights are independently resolved.

nonClaims: A catalog name match does not independently validate the fish or crustacean specimen identified in the EIS.
Candidate spelling variants do not justify silently correcting the EIS or asserting an identification.
The EIS taxon rows remain pooled across three named contexts; no fish can be assigned specifically to Julugan, Tanza, Kawit or Rosario from this crosscheck.

Nothing here establishes current presence, abundance, capture location, habitat use, local diet, bait effectiveness, catchability, safety, legal access, or completeness of Cavite or Manila Bay records.
WoRMS exact-query HTTP 204 results are limited to the exact query and API response at review time; they are not taxon-absence evidence.
nextActions: Search for a Cavite marine-fisheries source with per-site species allocation, fish-specific collection dates, gear and a traceable specimen/voucher crosswalk; retain the Julugan Tanza locality separately from Tanza Marine Tree Park.
Keep the EIS count conflict open: narrative reports 17 fish species while Table 2.27 contains 18 fish rows, including one genus-only row and both Sphyraena jello and Sphyraena sp.
